=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (four leaves are clearly attached at the same node, visible in multiple images, indicating a whorled arrangement)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped at the apex of the stem, with no other leaves visible along the stem below, indicating a clustered arrangement)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single, undivided blade with no leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)

C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins are smooth and uninterrupted across all visible leaves)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaves are elongated with a broad base tapering to a pointed tip)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tip is sharply pointed but not drawn out into a long tail)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (base is wedge-shaped, tapering to the petiole)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein runs from base to apex with secondary veins branching off and extending to the margin)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible, closely spaced, numerous (secondary veins are prominent and run perpendicular to the midrib, forming a reticulate pattern)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (surface is glossy and reflects light, likely due to moisture and cuticle)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or projections on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is short and not elongated, leaves appear sessile or nearly so)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petiole is round in cross-section, no wings or grooves visible)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (stem appears soft and green, typical of young seedlings)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem surface)
    19. Stem color: green (stem is uniformly green, with slight reddish-brown at base in some images)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (surface is smooth with no ridges or lenticels visible)

E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules observed at leaf base in any image)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no exudate seen upon stem or leaf damage)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen base at leaf petiole junction visible)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils observed)

F. Notes: Seedling appears healthy with no obvious damage. Leaves are arranged in a whorl of four at the apex. Stem is slender and green, consistent with a young seedling. Multiple images confirm the same individual from various angles, showing consistent morphology. The presence of a tag suggests it is part of a monitoring or research plot. No visible signs of herbivory or disease.
